chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiya said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The confined (al-mahsur) is not the blocked (al-masdud).' And he said: 'The confined is the sick person, and the blocked is the one whom the polytheists prevent, just as they prevented the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The blocked is not due to illness; women are permissible for him, but the confined, women are not permissible for him.'

key_terms.اَلْمَحْصُورُ: The confined one, specifically referring to a person prevented from completing Hajj/Umrah due to illness or internal impediment.
key_terms.اَلْمَصْدُودُ: The blocked one, referring to a person prevented by external forces (like polytheists) from completing the pilgrimage.
key_terms.اَلْمُشْرِكُونَ: The polytheists, specifically those who prevented the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from entering Mecca.
key_terms.تَحِلُّ لَهُ اَلنِّسَاءُ: Women are permissible for him, referring to the resumption of marital relations which are otherwise prohibited during Ihram.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the confined (mahsur) and the blocked (masdud) in Islamic jurisprudence regarding Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between 'al-mahsur' (confined by internal illness) and 'al-masdud' (blocked by external forces like polytheists), a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of marital relations during Ihram. This distinction highlights that the permissibility of resuming intimacy depends on whether the impediment is intrinsic to the pilgrim's body or extrinsic, reflecting the principle that external blockage does not carry the same prohibition as internal incapacity.
